[1/3] Rebuild a dead MCP server's client after a transport failure so later calls in the run work, without retrying the failed call

impact_assessment.why: The MCP hub is opened per run and a server that exits mid-run makes every later call fail for that run; ADR-018 recorded reconnect as deferred. Retrying the failed call blindly could duplicate a non-idempotent external side effect.
impact_assessment.benefits: A transient MCP server death no longer disables its tools for the rest of the run; the next call uses a freshly initialized client and re-registered tools, and the failed call is reported instead of silently replayed.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: hub internal behavior and error text; dependency: none; concurrency: one server's client is replaced while other servers stay live; state: no persistence, and the failed call is intentionally not retried
impact_assessment.mitigation: fixture sentinel kills the server; fail-first test asserts the failed call, the reconnect note, and a successful next call through the effect ledger; all stdio/HTTP/SSE MCP tests plus full gates

description: [milestone 1/6] Wave 0 of the engine-depth plan: the gaps are now machine-runnable rather than prose. Added tests/integration/engine-gaps.test.ts (13 tests: 6 pass, 7 it.fails pinning verified gaps), scripts/engine-gaps.ts (npm run engine:gaps) and a frozen evals/results/baselines/engine-baseline-v1.json. Re-verification corrected plan v1 twice: CRLF/BOM preservation already works end to end and is NOT a gap, and the missing tool history is deeper than a mapper bug because appendMessage only accepts user|assistant so tool results never enter the message store. 624 tests pass, typecheck and lint clean.

[1/6] Engine-depth plan: pin each verified gap, then close them wave by wave. Waves: (0) failing-fast tests + measured baseline, done in this commit; (1) derive the compaction budget from the model window, add an LLM summariser with mechanical fallback, re-inject an artifact manifest, and give the message store a tool role so a resumed run sees its tool results; (2) edit-match cascade for indentation and CRLF/LF, plus a read ledger with stale-write refusal reusing the FILE_CONFLICT pattern; (3) parallel read batches and real background shells; (4) per-step retry and a normalised doom-loop signature; (5) CLI parity (-p, --model, stdin, --no-session, -r, finer exit codes). CRLF/BOM serialisation is already correct and is excluded.

impact_assessment.why: The engine cannot hold a real repository in context (24k compaction against a 200k-1M window), cannot heal ordinary model drift in edits, can clobber a file it never read, and forgets its own tool results on resume. These are the gaps that stop real work completing; tool breadth and UI are not the constraint.
impact_assessment.benefits: A run can use the window the model actually has, a resumed run keeps its tool history, edits stop being refused over whitespace, and an unread or externally changed file cannot be silently overwritten.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: data-testid, exit codes and docs/FEATURES.md are pinned claims; dependency: none added; concurrency: parallel reads share the effect ledger and approval prompts; state: a model-backed summariser adds a provider call that costs tokens and can fail, and a message-store role change needs a schema migration
impact_assessment.mitigation: Summariser failure degrades to the mechanical path rather than blocking a run; the schema change is additive with a version bump; parallel execution is restricted to read-only batches; every wave is re-measured against engine-baseline-v1.json and a wave with no paired numbers is not counted as done

(2) Edit/write correctness: edits.ts matches the exact substring first then heals CRLF/LF, trailing-whitespace or indentation drift over whole-line windows and reports the strategy; server/readLedger.ts refuses a full overwrite of a file this run has not read or that changed since, and refuses a targeted edit of a file that changed since (its oldString already pins the content). description: [1/1] Bound the read ledger's second cache. description: [1/2] Reopen a conversation over ACP and let an editor choose its mode. description: [1/1] Make stopping a run stop its in-flight shell. Analysed projects/harness against atelier: most of the harness's ideas are already here (the r0-r9 ladder including injection refusal, budget death and hallucinated-tool refusal; doom-loop detection; bounded logs; artifact spill; provider failover), but its runner polls the stop switch while a child process runs and kills it, and atelier does not. stopSessionRun aborts the run's AbortController, yet runShell has no signal, so a running bash call (timeoutMs up to 600000) keeps running after the UI says stopped and executeRun stays pending until it exits. Thread the run's signal through executeTool into runShell: on abort kill the process tree, resolve the tool with 'stopped by stop request', and return the run as blocked with reason stopped as soon as the tool result is recorded. Test-first: an aborted run settles in seconds instead of waiting for its 30 s command, and a normal command still completes.

impact_assessment.why: Harness analysis found one capability gap that matters for a local agent: a stop that leaves the command it started running is not a stop, and the run stays pending behind it.
impact_assessment.benefits: Stop means stop for foreground commands too; the run settles in seconds, the process tree is killed, and the transcript records why the call ended.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: executeTool gains an optional signal argument and ToolContext an optional signal field, both backwards compatible; dependency: none; concurrency: an abort listener per shell call, removed when it settles; state: one extra tool.result output line (stopped by stop request)
impact_assessment.mitigation: Test-first at both levels (executeTool with a signal and a real run stopped through stopSessionRun); killing reuses the existing taskkill process-tree helper; a normal command and the existing timeout path are re-run by the full suite

description: [1/1] Stop a run that keeps failing tool calls with different inputs. Fresh harness-vs-atelier pass after the harness reforge: atelier's only loop guard is the doom loop, which fires on an identical call signature (name plus JSON input), so a model that retries with slightly different arguments can burn every step and dollar on calls that all fail (unknown tool, disabled tool, denied approval, a tool exception). Harness stops such a run: its loop counts consecutive failed results and ends the run after two, resetting on any success. Port that guard with a limit of three (atelier's default doomLoopLimit), counting only tool outcomes with ok=false so a failing test command (exit 1, ok=true) never trips it and the fail-fix-test loop still works. Test-first: a run whose model makes three different failing calls ends blocked with a consecutive-failures reason after exactly three tool results, while failures separated by one successful call finish normally.

impact_assessment.why: Fresh harness-vs-atelier pass after the reforge: atelier stops identical repeated calls but not a spiral of different calls that all fail, so a model can burn its whole step and dollar budget on errors.
impact_assessment.benefits: A run that is not converging ends early with a clear reason after three failed calls in a row, and stops costing money; successful calls (including a failing test command, which is a successful tool call) reset the count, so the fail-fix-test loop is untouched.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: one new blocked reason (consecutive tool failures) on the run row and session event; dependency: none; concurrency: the counter is local to the run loop; state: no schema change, no new persistence
impact_assessment.mitigation: Test-first with a fixture provider: three different unknown-tool calls must block after exactly three results, and a failure-success-failure sequence must finish; the constant sits beside the doom-loop check in the same loop; the full suite and gates run after
